title: A05 JSON and nested data with explode cheat sheet
subtitle: ASSOCIATE EXAM PREP · A05 · SECTION 2 (21%) + SECTION 3 (22%) · NESTED JSON QUICK REFERENCE

pages.title: A05 · JSON and nested data with explode
lede: Objectives: ingest semi-structured data (JSON and nested data) into Unity Catalog governed Delta tables (S2); manipulate columns and rows, including exploding arrays (S3).
Free Edition: Unity Catalog volume source, serverless notebook. Fictional orders only.

blocks.heading: 1. Read JSON: inferred or explicit schema
blocks.code:
raw_df = spark.read.json(src)                       # JSON Lines: one record per line (default)
spark.read.option("multiLine", "true").json(path)     # pretty-printed file spanning lines
orders = spark.read.schema(schema_ddl).json(src)    # explicit: no inference pass, your types
blocks.note: Inference: whole numbers -> long, decimals -> double, field names sorted. Auto Loader infers JSON as strings unless cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes.

blocks.heading: 2. Nested types in a DDL schema
blocks.code:
order_id INT,
customer STRUCT<name: STRING, address: STRUCT<city: STRING, country: STRING>>,
items    ARRAY<STRUCT<sku: STRING, qty: INT, price: DECIMAL(10,2)>>,
tags     ARRAY<STRING>

blocks.heading: 3. Structs: dot notation (row count unchanged)
blocks.code:
orders.select("order_id", "customer.name", col("customer.address.city").alias("city"))
orders.select("order_id", "customer.*")              # every struct field as a column
blocks.note: The new column takes the last field name (name, city). Alias it when names could clash.

blocks.heading: 4. Arrays: explode family (row count changes)
blocks.code:
explode("items")         1 row per element; null or [] array -> NO row
explode_outer("items")   same, but null or [] -> 1 row with a null element
posexplode("items")      columns pos + col, pos starts at 0; skips null or []
posexplode_outer(...)    position + keeps null or []
explode(map_col)         columns key + value
blocks.note: Other selected columns (order_id) repeat on every exploded row.

pages.title: Flatten, from_json, SQL colon syntax, exam traps

blocks.heading: 5. Worked example: 4 orders
blocks.code:
1001 [A1, B2]  1002 [C3]  1003 []  1004 null
explode -> 3 rows   explode_outer -> 5 rows   posexplode 1001 -> pos 0, 1

blocks.heading: 7. JSON in a string column: from_json
blocks.note: schema_of_json(sample) derives a schema from a sample JSON string.

blocks.heading: 8. Databricks SQL
blocks.code:
SELECT value:customer.address.city, value:items[0].sku, value:items[*].sku,
       value:order_id::int FROM raw_orders          -- colon syntax on JSON strings
SELECT o.order_id, i.item.sku FROM orders_bronze AS o,
       LATERAL explode(o.items) AS i(item)          -- explode as a table reference
blocks.note: Colon results are strings (cast with ::). [*] is for JSON strings only. SELECT-list explode and LATERAL VIEW are deprecated.

blocks.heading: 9. Five exam traps
blocks.text: 1) explode drops rows whose array is null or empty. 2) explode_outer keeps them with a null element. 3) posexplode returns pos and col, and pos starts at 0. 4) Pretty-printed JSON needs multiLine = true. 5) The JSON reader infers real types; Auto Loader infers JSON columns as strings unless cloudFiles.inferColumnTypes.

blocks.heading: Practice challenge
blocks.text: tags: 1001 [web, promo], 1002 [store], 1003 [], 1004 [web]. explode(tags) -> 4 rows. explode_outer(tags) -> 5 rows (1003 kept with null). posexplode: promo is pos 1 (web is 0).
